inspection_summary: Inspected all 753 normalized lines. The source develops two complementary functional-equation contour geometries, uses the Lambda-contour magnitude to distinguish symmetric zero derivatives, and proves a uniform modified Gram-point mean for Re zeta by converting an approximate functional equation into cosine sums controlled through phase curvature. Formula extraction is imperfect but the prose and surviving displays jointly recover the selected mechanisms; plot-only numerical detail is treated as supporting evidence rather than exact data.

accepted_units.title: Functional-equation phases turn critical-line zeta values into real data
accepted_units.why_material: The source relates xi, Phi, Lambda, theta, Z, and Gram points so that phase normalization makes Z real and identifies Gram ordinates as locations where zeta is real. This is the representation layer used by every later contour and averaging claim.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the local definitions and both displayed forms of the functional equation; no external convention is needed beyond the checked span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the surviving displayed formulas for Phi, theta, Z, and Lambda; the accompanying prose resolves the degraded fraction typography.

accepted_units.title: A compensating functional-equation term extends the Gram-point mean across sigma > 0
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 1 identifies the sigma-dependent main term that must be subtracted from Re zeta at Gram ordinates, gives a uniform error, and explains both geometric robustness of the sampling path and the unproved numerical suggestion of extension left of the critical strip.
accepted_units.context_note: Uses Gram points and Lambda already defined in unit u01; this span includes the theorem, limiting consequence, sampling-path comment, and explicit boundary of the proved result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact correction and error exponents are display-dependent and should be checked against the retained PDF before symbol-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Positivity on a Gram line would rigidify an argument-principle zero count
accepted_units.why_material: The source turns positivity of Re zeta along a horizontal boundary segment into a single-valued logarithm and a bounded argument variation, forcing the zero count to be the nearest integer to the theta main term. It then isolates infinitely many Gram lines with this positivity as the motivating target.
accepted_units.context_note: The conclusion is explicitly a research objective supported by later average evidence, not a theorem proved in this paper.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires the contour-integral display and nearest-integer expression; prose preserves the logical implication despite imperfect mathematical glyph extraction.

accepted_units.title: Lambda-real contours pair by reflection and classify critical-line crossings
accepted_units.why_material: The functional identity Lambda(s)Lambda(1-s)=1 forces reflection symmetry of real-Lambda contours and values ±1 on their critical-line crossings. Those signs distinguish real from imaginary zeta values and center from node behavior at simple zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains Lemma 2 and its proof, including the nonvanishing statement away from the real axis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies on conjugation bars and real/imaginary-part glyphs that are degraded in extraction; the checked prose makes their roles recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Lambda-real contours are asymptotically horizontal Gram lines
accepted_units.why_material: A Stirling expansion converts the implicit reality condition for Lambda into contour equations, showing O(1/t) departure from horizontal intervals and an even/odd split between Gram and imaginary-zeta crossings.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof deliberately records the expansion strategy rather than every manipulation, and the closing theta expansion checks the Gram-point specialization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly display-dependent: exact coefficients, parity, and O-terms require the retained source image for downstream transcription, while the geometric conclusion is clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Magnitude of Lambda varies monotonically along its real contours
accepted_units.why_material: Factoring Re Lambda into a positive exponential amplitude and a cosine phase shows that on a real-Lambda contour the phase is asymptotically pinned to an integer multiple of pi while the amplitude grows with sigma. This yields strict monotonicity and an explicit signed asymptotic.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the related off-contour imaginary-part asymptotic in the remark because it clarifies the phase representation used later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The factorization and signed power asymptotic depend on formula layout; prose supplies the monotonicity argument but exact constants merit scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Reflected off-critical zeros cannot have equal derivative magnitude
accepted_units.why_material: Differentiating the functional equation to the zero multiplicity transfers derivatives between reflected zeros with multiplier Lambda. The contour magnitude estimate then makes the derivative magnitude strictly asymmetric on opposite sides of the critical line.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed proof states a sufficient height condition while the lemma is phrased for positive ordinate; preserve that proof-local qualification when reusing the claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on superscript derivative notation and the asymptotic modulus of Lambda, both readable but extraction-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Phi-real contours meet Gram points with a small nonhorizontal angle
accepted_units.why_material: The source contrasts the two functional-equation multipliers: Phi-real contours cross the same Gram points as Lambda-real contours but have asymptotic slope -pi/(2 log t), with O(1/t) deviation from the corresponding tilted intervals.
accepted_units.context_note: Lemma 6 supplies the phase-difference estimate used to interpret the geometry; Lemma 7 derives the critical-line crossing from Phi(1/2+it) being real and refers back to the earlier Stirling method.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact implicit contour coefficients and the angle require display verification; the contrast with horizontal Lambda contours is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Modified Gram-point means expose cosine sums as the analytic bottleneck
accepted_units.why_material: The modified averages numerically approach one across sampled sigma values, and the text immediately isolates a uniform cosine-sum estimate over Gram ordinates as the needed analytic control. This links empirical normalization to the proof mechanism without treating the plot as proof.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the plot extraction and Lemma 8 statement; the proof is separated as unit u10.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The numerical curves and labels are figure-dependent and only partially linearized; the claimed 5120-point agreement and the cosine-sum bound are recoverable from prose and display.

accepted_units.title: Phase curvature at Gram ordinates yields square-root cancellation
accepted_units.why_material: Extending the Gram index continuously turns the oscillation into a phase phi(nu). Theta asymptotics give a positive lower bound for -phi'', allowing a van der Corput-type estimate and hence an O(N^(1/2) log N) cosine-sum bound with absolute constant.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the complete source-given proof of Lemma 8, including why dependence on log n can be made uniform for integers n at least two.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires accurate derivative and asymptotic displays; the proof narrative fixes the sign, curvature role, and final order even where primes are degraded.

accepted_units.title: The Dirichlet-series regime controls modified means to the right of one
accepted_units.why_material: The first regime of Theorem 1 expands zeta where sigma exceeds a tunable threshold and applies the Gram-ordinate cosine estimate termwise, producing a bound controlled by the distance of that threshold from one.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the restated theorem so the target estimate is locally visible; later units handle 0 < sigma below the threshold and optimize it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact exponents in the theorem and regime bound are formula-dependent and need source-image verification before machine parsing.

accepted_units.title: The approximate functional equation reduces the left regime to two cosine sums
accepted_units.why_material: For 0 < sigma below the transition, the approximate functional equation and the Gram-line asymptotics for chi separate the modified real zeta value into two truncated cosine sums F1 and F2 plus a controlled aggregate error. The functional-equation correction appears naturally as the second main term.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly absorbs the sine contribution and several smaller errors into one error term; units u13-u14 bound the two surviving sums and combine regimes.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly dependent on multi-line displays and OCR-fragile exponents; the decomposition's structure is clear, but exact formula ingestion requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Reordering and partial summation transfer the cosine bound to F1 and F2
accepted_units.why_material: The proof reorders the moving truncation using a threshold tau to bound F1 directly, then applies weighted partial summation through t(x)=x/log x to control F2. This demonstrates how one oscillatory estimate survives two differently weighted pieces of the functional equation.
accepted_units.context_note: The F2 derivation continues through line 650; the subsequent parameter optimization is isolated in unit u14.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Nested sums, powers, and integration limits are extraction-sensitive; exact inequalities should be checked against the PDF, while the reordering and partial-summation mechanism is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Optimizing the transition parameter makes the average estimate uniform in sigma
accepted_units.why_material: The source packages competing error terms into g_N(x), chooses the unique minimizing transition sigma_N, and splits the sigma range so that the high- and low-sigma estimates combine into the theorem's uniform bound.
accepted_units.context_note: This span is the final optimization and assembly step of Theorem 1; it also explains absorption of finitely many omitted initial terms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The minimizer and piecewise exponents are display-dependent; source-image checking is required for exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: Average positivity gives infinitely many positive Gram-point values, but leftward extension remains conjectural
accepted_units.why_material: The proved error estimate yields convergence of the modified average, a linear lower bound for the sum of real parts, and therefore infinitely many positive values at Gram ordinates for each fixed 0 < sigma < 1. The authors separately mark sigma = 0 and further-left extension as numerical conjecture.
accepted_units.context_note: The positivity conclusion concerns point values at Gram ordinates; it does not establish positivity along entire Gram lines or the motivating zero-count objective in unit u03.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Corollary formulas are readable but exponent and limit notation remain OCR-sensitive; the prose preserves the quantifiers and proved-versus-conjectured boundary.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Complementary functional-equation foliations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The Lambda and Phi multipliers encode the same Gram-point phase constraint through geometrically different real contours: Lambda supplies nearly horizontal, magnitude-monotone lines, whereas Phi supplies slightly tilted lines through the same critical-line points.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is an internal comparison of the source's asymptotic contour descriptions; it does not show that either foliation alone controls zeta zeros or proves the motivating positivity property.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From phase curvature to a uniform modified mean
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The proof pipeline uses curvature of the continuously indexed Gram phase to obtain cancellation, inserts that cancellation into both sides of an approximate functional equation, and optimizes a sigma transition to make the corrected average uniform over the open right half-plane.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The cancellation and final estimate are solver-independent analytic claims in this source, but exact exponent transcription remains formula-sensitive and the result excludes sigma at or left of zero.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Average positivity versus the zero-count objective
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The mean theorem guarantees infinitely many positive point values on each fixed vertical sampling line, offering partial evidence for the positivity phenomenon that would make the argument-principle zero count rigid.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Positive values at isolated Gram ordinates do not imply positivity along the full boundary intervals required by the motivating nearest-integer criterion.
